Does 'between two consonants' require the consonants to be immediately adjacent to the vowel, or can there be other characters in between?
When scanning 'from the right side', do we return the first vowel (from right) that meets the condition, or the vowel closest to the right end in terms of position?
Is the word guaranteed to be at least one character long?
Should the function treat uppercase and lowercase letters as distinct for vowel/consonant classification?
What constitutes a consonant? Is it any letter that is not a vowel, or are there special cases?
Does 'between two consonants' require the consonants to be different letters, or can they be the same?
If a vowel is between two consonants but one of those consonants is at the beginning or end of the word, does it count?
answers: Only 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u' and their uppercase versions are vowels; 'y' and 'Y' are consonants.

A consonant is any English letter not in the vowel set.
They can be the same or different; only that both are consonants matters.
No, vowels at the beginning or end of the word do not count, as per the specification.
